name: Do I need to prime the drywall patch before painting?

mainEntity.name: Do I need to prime the drywall patch before painting?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it is highly recommended to prime a drywall patch before painting. Primer serves several important functions: it seals the porous surface of the new joint compound, ensuring uniform paint absorption and preventing a dull or uneven finish. It also helps to prevent 'flashing,' where the patch area appears different in sheen or color than the surrounding painted wall. Priming creates a consistent base, allowing your topcoat paint to adhere better and achieve a uniform, professional-looking result.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, priming drywall patches is crucial. It seals the compound, ensures uniform paint absorption, prevents flashing, and creates a consistent base for painting.
